summary: Cold read of the recorded drill-transactions-view contract and task plan (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only) returned NOT CONVERGED with seven findings, including a contradiction that made the recorded criterion impossible to satisfy. All seven were answerable from the repository and folded into the contract and task plan; required leaves went from seven to ten. Nothing needed the human beyond the closing round.

criteria_map.Leaf Actuals become activatable in BOTH: Leaf affordance and in-panel navigation. The cold read found aggregate-to-leaf navigation entirely unspecified: the panel restores focus only to its statement opener, so drilling a leaf from inside it could leave focus on an unmounted control and force a close/reopen. The criterion now specifies an in-place body swap, a Back control on the breadcrumb group crumb (the prototype's own drill.toGroup seam) returning focus to the leaf row used, and Close returning to the still-mounted statement button.
criteria_map.The request is built from the DISPLAYED: Request construction. Unchanged by the grill: built from the resolved response rather than the mutable selectors, with provenance.activeBatchIds passed through verbatim so the server's completeness rule cannot be turned into a silently wrong footer.
criteria_map.The transactions state renders the serve: The table. The cold read found the plan omitted both a date-display rule and the column-layout migration: the server sends date-only strings that would repeat the ISO-label defect if rendered raw, and .mis-drill-table's positional rules encode the SIX-column aggregate layout. The criterion now requires UTC-safe formatting and dedicated styling for the seven-column table.
criteria_map.Pagination is server-side and the client: Pagination. The cold read found 'keep the reader oriented' had no policy and no proof. The criterion now states it: navigation disabled while pending, the previous successful page visible with a loading indication, and a terminal refusal clearing the rows, count and footer so stale numbers never sit beside an error.
criteria_map.Every server outcome has exactly ONE cle: Outcome states. The cold read found two gaps: batchStatuses is a LIST and an FY-YTD drill can carry several replaced batches, so a find() would render one and hide the rest; and the exact-paise footing the confirmed spec requires was never checked on the client. The criterion now requires every replaced source and period to be named, and the displayed footer to be checked against the clicked leaf's Actual in paise with a withheld state on mismatch.
criteria_map.The behaviour is proven by vitest leaves: Proofs. The cold read found the recorded criterion impossible to satisfy - it required a live paged drill while no real leaf exceeds 18 rows - and that not one required leaf touched the api client, so the route, CSRF header, retry-on-401 and untouched payload were unproven by construction. The criterion now splits the pagination proof (fabricated response) from the live check (no paging, and the evidence says so), adds a direct api.test.ts leaf, and re-asserts task 2's zero-network proof as a required leaf of THIS task so regressing decision 0024 fails here.

current_flow: Task 1 shipped POST api/mis/statement/drill with its wire types; task 2 shipped the drill panel, but only for aggregates - it is a pure client projection of the statement payload with a required test spying the api client and asserting zero calls. statement-view.tsx passes onOpen only when a node has children, so leaf Actuals are plain text, and the panel's own leaf rows are plain text too; the prototype's 'Click any Actual to see its transactions' copy was deliberately withheld. No frontend code calls the drill endpoint. This task is the first and only consumer of it.
new_abstractions: A second body state inside the existing panel, with its own data lifecycle - request, pending, pagination and five terminal outcomes - where task 2's panel had exactly one synchronous state.
In-place navigation between the aggregate and leaf states, with a Back seam and an explicit focus contract across a body swap.
A direct api-client test for the drill route, establishing that route, CSRF and retry behaviour are proven outside the component tests that mock them.
gaps: Aggregate-to-leaf navigation was unspecified: the panel restores focus only to its original statement opener on unmount, while the prototype offers a return-to-group interaction, so drilling a leaf from inside the panel had no defined Back action, focus target or Close behaviour and focus could land on an unmounted leaf button.

The plan promised an api-client method and test but no required leaf executed frontend/src/lib/api.test.ts; the component leaves mock the client, so the route path, the CSRF header, the retry-on-401 and the untouched pinned payload were unprovable by construction. Task 2's zero-network aggregate proof was also merely hoped to survive rather than required here.
'Keep the reader oriented' during a page request had no state policy and no proof, leaving stale rows, counts and a footer free to remain beside an error.

Exact-paise footing is required by the confirmed spec, but the proposed leaves only proved that a response footer is displayed - not that it equals the clicked leaf's Actual, and with no defined behaviour when it does not.
Replacement notices were underspecified for FY-YTD: batchStatuses is per pinned batch and several can be replaced at once, so a singular find() would name one and hide the rest.

The plan omitted the client date-display rule and the seven-column layout migration: the server supplies date-only strings that would repeat the established ISO-label defect if rendered raw, and the existing .mis-drill-table positional styles encode the six-column aggregate layout.
contradictions: The recorded criterion required a live functional check that pages a result larger than one page, while the task plan's own grounding establishes that the largest (plant, cost centre, GL) group in the client's July extract is 18 rows - so no real leaf can reach the server's fixed 100-row page and the contract was impossible to satisfy as written.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dtv-c1 now specifies the in-place body swap, the Back control on the breadcrumb group crumb (the prototype's own drill.toGroup seam) returning focus to the leaf row used, and Close returning focus to the statement button that stays mounted throughout; a required leaf covers open-aggregate, drill-leaf, back, close.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dtv-c6 adds a required leaf in frontend/src/lib/api.test.ts driving the client directly (following the existing pattern at api.test.ts:52), and re-asserts task 2's zero-network aggregate proof as a required leaf of this task.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dtv-c4 states the pending policy explicitly: navigation disabled, the previous successful page visible with a loading indication, and a terminal refusal or failure clearing the rows, count and footer; a required leaf drives success then pending then failure.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dtv-c5 requires the displayed footer to be checked against the clicked leaf's Actual in exact paise, withholding the total in the treatment task 2 established when it does not match.
REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dtv-c5 requires every replaced source and period to be rendered from the batchStatuses list, never a find(), with a multi-replacement required leaf.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dtv-c3 requires UTC-safe formatting of the date-only month and postingDate strings (parsed at UTC midnight as statement-view already does) and dedicated column styling for the seven-column table, because the existing .mis-drill-table positional rules encode the six-column aggregate layout.

REPO-ANSWERED - the impossible criterion is split: pagination is proven against a fabricated response in the vitest leaves, and the live check explicitly does NOT page, with the evidence stating why (the July extract's largest group is 18 rows). This is the same class as the FY-YTD fixture task 1 needed.
open_items: Non-blocking - required leaves rose from seven to ten and the review budget to 8 files / 1500 lines, recorded with its reason: most of the additions are state-machine cases that exist only in this task.

rounds.question: Closing the drill-transactions-view task grill. Seven findings, all answerable from the repo, so nothing here needs your judgement — but two are worth knowing about. **My recorded criterion was impossible to satisfy**: it required a live drill of more than 100 rows, while the largest real leaf in the July extract is 18 — so pagination is now proven against a fabricated response and the live check explicitly does not page. And **none of the seven required tests touched the API client**: component tests mock it, so the route, the CSRF header, the retry-on-401 and the untouched pinned payload were all unproven; there is now a required leaf in `api.test.ts`, plus task 2's zero-network proof re-asserted as a required leaf here so regressing decision 0024 fails this task. Also settled: in-panel leaf drilling swaps the body in place with a Back control on the breadcrumb (the prototype's own seam) and a focus contract that can't land on an unmounted button; every replaced batch is named rather than the first `find()`; pending is a state with rules (navigation disabled, previous page visible, failure clears it); and the dates are UTC-safe with the seven-column table getting its own styling, since the existing positional CSS encodes the six-column layout. Any remaining gap before this goes to the board?
